HDB unveils plans for new Pasir Ris neighbourhood; 13ha of natural habitats to be retained
article:
HDB has announced plans for a new neighbourhood comprising a mix of public and private homes along Pasir Ris Drive 4.

The proposed neighbourhood will be “set amidst greenery, with amenities and community spaces for residents to enjoy”, said HDB in a Facebook post on Nov 23.

It is expected to provide more housing options in the area, which has seen strong demand for recent Build-To-Order projects, including Costa Grove and Costa Riviera I and II, the government agency added.

The proposed neighbourhood sits on a forested site fronting Sungei Loyang that is adjacent to mangroves and other vegetation along the coast, facing Serangoon Harbour. The site has been zoned predominantly for residential use since URA’s Master Plan 1980.

In planning for the new homes, HDB said it had assessed alternative brownfield sites nearby, such as the former Siglap Secondary School site, as well as industrial sites at Lorong Halus.

“However, these sites are already being planned for future housing supply, needed for other national uses, or cannot be made available within the timeframe required,” HDB noted.

It added that there are “no suitable alternative brownfield sites available within the next few years that can provide a comparable amount of housing” to the site at Pasir Ris Drive 4.

Following an environmental impact assessment, HDB is proposing to retain 13ha of existing nature.

The areas that will be retained include 8ha of intertidal, seagrass and mangrove habitats, as well as 5ha of vegetation. The latter will serve as a buffer between the housing development, and the mangroves and an existing stream.

The new neighbourhood will also introduce a 15m-wide linear park along Sungei Loyang and green buffers along the northern, western and southern edges of the site to create walking trails for residents.

HDB added that it will implement an environmental monitoring and management plan to guide construction activities and manage potential impact on the surrounding habitat.

“Together, these measures will help us plan sensitively around the site's important ecological features while meeting Singaporeans’ housing needs,” it said.

title: S$50,000 in These 4 REITs: How Much Passive Income Could You Receive?
article:
S$50,000 is enough to form a meaningful foundation for an income-focused portfolio, and
Singapore real estate investment trusts
(REITs) are a natural place to put it.
They’re popular because they pass on recurring distributions backed by real rental income, not just a promise.
But how much income that S$50,000 actually generates depends on more than finding high-yielding names.
Distribution sustainability, debt costs, occupancy, rental reversions and the quality of the underlying properties all shape whether today’s yield survives next year.
How Much Passive Income Can S$50,000 Generate?
The maths is simple: a 4% yield pays S$2,000 a year, a 6% yield pays S$3,000; the higher the yield, the higher the income and vice versa.
However, these numbers are illustrative only ­– actual income depends on the price you actually pay and on distributions that can rise or fall, and REITs don’t necessarily pay the same distribution per unit (DPU) each quarter.
CapitaLand Integrated Commercial Trust (SGX: C38U), or CICT – The Core Income Anchor
Singapore’s largest REIT
owns retail and office assets in prime locations such as Raffles City, Plaza Singapura and Capital Tower.
As of 30 September 2026, overall portfolio occupancy was resilient at 96.1%, with rental reversions of 4.6% (retail) and 7.1% (office).
The balance sheet is healthy, with gearing at a manageable 39.7
%
, while its interest coverage ratio (ICR) is comfortable at 3.8x.
For the first half ended 30 June 2026 (1H2026), DPU grew 7.1% year on year (YoY) to
S$0.0602
,
even after a dilutive placement of new units; last 12 months (LTM) annualised yield works out to roughly 5.1%.
CICT’s latest DPU growth continues a solid trend of generally increasing DPU over the past five years.
S$12,500 allocated to this name could generate annual income of S$637.50; since 2021, CICT has typically paid distributions twice or three times a year.
Keppel DC REIT (SGX: AJBU), or KDCREIT – The Growth REIT
Next, Singapore’s largest pure-play data centre REIT offers income investors exposure to the secular growth trend of cloud computing and AI.
With 27 data centres spanning 10 countries and a proven appetite for accretive acquisitions, the growth runway for KDCREIT looks bright.
For the nine months ended 30 September 2026 (9M2026), distributable income rose 16.7% YoY to S$228.0 million, and DPU grew 11.7% YoY to S$0.08571.
The data centre REIT’s performance was aided by resilient occupancy of 93.0% and positive rental reversions of about 14% in 9M2026.
Having
Keppel Ltd
(SGX: BN4) as a sponsor also affords KDCREIT a healthy pipeline of potential new data centres to acquire.
Importantly, the debt profile appears relatively well-staggered, with a weighted average debt tenor of 3.1 years.
At an LTM distribution yield of 4.9%, S$12,500 brings you S$612.50 in annual income.
Given we are just in the early innings of AI, there is plenty of room for KDCREIT to grow its DPU and your income over time.
Parkway Life REIT (SGX: C2PU), or PLife REIT – The Defensive REIT
PLife REIT offers some defensiveness to a REIT portfolio.
Owning hospitals and nursing homes across Singapore, Japan and France, this REIT stands out for its uninterrupted DPU growth every year since its 2007 IPO.
This feat is only possible due to its long-term lease contracts, backed by assets that enjoy resilient demand no matter what the economy is doing.
Do note that its top tenant, Parkway Hospitals Singapore, contributes about 68% of gross revenue.
3Q2026 numbers confirm the story: as at 30 September 2026, committed occupancy stood at 100% in Singapore and France and 94.3% in Japan, with a weighted average lease to expiry (WALE) of 14.43 years.
Finally, the balance sheet is rock-solid, with a gearing of 34.8% and an ICR of 7.9x.
9M2026 DPU rose 13.4% YoY to S$0.1310.
Parkway Life’s LTM yield sits at 3.9%, providing S$487.50 in annual income, and its record suggests that income has been reliable.
Sasseur REIT (SGX: CRPU), or Sasseur – The Higher-Yield REIT
Sasseur operates four outlet malls in China – two in Chongqing and one each in Hefei and Kunming – with rent partly linked to tenant sales.
Portfolio tenant sales rose 4.4% YoY to RMB3.39 billion in 9M2026, with Chongqing Liangjiang posting record nine-month sales.
At roughly 9.7% (LTM), the yield is well above the other three – yet the balance sheet is unusually strong for that yield: gearing of 25.3
%
, cost of debt down to 3.6
%
, weighted average debt maturity extended to 4.6 years and an ICR of 6.8x.
Its assets seem stable, with an occupancy rate of 98.6% as at 30 September 2026
.
The yield is partly explained by a shorter WALE (1.9 years by net lettable area and 1.1 years by gross revenue), a “China discount” and the fear of a slowdown in overall consumption in China.
A 10.2% yield generates S$1,275 in annual income, but the China-related risks are something to be weighed against.
What Could S$50,000 Generate Across the Four REITs?
Assume an equal S$12,500 in each:

This portfolio works out to roughly S$251 a month on average, though actual distributions vary given the REITs’ different distribution schedules.
The blended yield here matters more than any single REIT’s number: Sasseur’s high yield lifts the average and supplies about 42% of the income, so the portfolio leans on its highest-risk REIT; the other three provide the steadier base.
Could the Income Grow Over Time?
Portfolio income can grow in two ways.
The first is DPU growth from positive rental reversions, rising occupancy, acquisitions or falling borrowing costs, which Keppel DC REIT and Parkway Life REIT are already delivering.
The second is reinvesting distributions, which buys more units that generate their own payouts.
Consider this: if the portfolio’s 6% yield were fully reinvested every year at unchanged unit prices, S$50,000 could grow to about S$89,500 after 10 years, generating around S$5,400 a year in income.
Any DPU growth would add to that.
This is hypothetical, but it shows why growth and reinvestment matter more than chasing today’s highest single yield.
What Could Reduce the S$50,000 Income Stream?
DPU cuts, higher rates pushing up refinancing costs, falling occupancy, negative reversions, declining asset values, a dilutive rights issue or weakening tenant demand could pressure income generation.
Also, do note that REIT distributions are never guaranteed; income investors need to keep checking the portfolio and balance sheet, not just collect the cheque.
Get Smart: Build Income, Not Just Yield
S$50,000 spread across these four REITs could generate roughly S$3,000 a year today – a solid, diversified starting income.
But the headline number is only the starting point. What actually matters is whether each REIT can maintain its DPU, manage its debt and keep growing rental income through changing conditions.
Over time,
DPU growth
and reinvestment can turn a modest initial stake into a meaningfully larger income-producing portfolio.

title: Coca-Cola HBC rises in JSE debut ahead of US$2.6 bil deal
article:
(Nov 23): Coca-Cola HBC AG rose in its Johannesburg trading debut, adding one of the world’s biggest bottlers of the beverage to Africa’s largest stock exchange days before it completes a US$2.6 billion acquisition that will significantly expand its presence on the continent.

The shares opened at 996 rand on the city’s main bourse and traded at almost 1,015 rand by 9:14am.

A praise singer wearing a red beaded traditional hat blew a kudu horn and beat a huge drum at the exchange, which had Coca-Cola’s trademark red branding displayed on boards throughout the bourse.

Unlike an initial public offering, Coca-Cola HBC’s debut is a secondary listing by introduction of its existing shares and doesn’t involve an offer or raising new capital. The company’s primary listing remains in London, with its shares also traded in Athens.

The Johannesburg debut comes days before Coca-Cola HBC is expected to complete its purchase of a 75% stake in Coca-Cola Beverages Africa (Pty) Ltd from Coca-Cola Co and Gutsche Family Investments. The US$2.6 billion transaction, announced last year, will create the world’s second-biggest bottling partner of the beverage by volume and substantially increase its exposure to fast-growing African markets.

As part of the acquisition, Coca-Cola HBC will issue 21 million new shares to Gutsche Family Investments when the deal is expected to close on Nov 27. They are due to begin trading in Johannesburg, London and Athens on Nov 30.

See also: India stocks erase yearly losses as foreign buying spurs rebound

Following completion, Kar-Tess Holding — an investment vehicle linked to the family of Coca-Cola HBC chairman Anastassis David — will own 22.14% of the company, while Coca-Cola Co will hold 20.3% and Gutsche Family Investments 5.45%.

The transaction is part of Coca-Cola Co’s longstanding strategy of reducing direct ownership of bottling operations while retaining stakes in major bottling partners.

The listing adds a company valued at about 370 billion rand (US$21 billion) to the JSE after years declines. The exchange ended 2025 with 271 listings, down from 284 two years earlier, according to South African Reserve Bank data.

title: French companies to announce €14.9 bil in investments
article:
(Nov 23): The French government said that local companies are set to announce 81 new projects on Monday (Nov 23) for a total of €14.9 billion.

The investments, ranging from factory construction or expansion projects to funding rounds, are due to be showcased in Paris during the Choose France conference for domestic companies. The government said in a press release that it will present a wider number of projects carried out or decided upon in 2026, bringing the total to €42.5 billion.

Among the projects highlighted are tentative plans by Groupe ADP — which still need board approval — to invest €9.5 billion in France to overhaul Paris-Charles de Gaulle and Paris-Orly airports.

Finance Minister Roland Lescure said that nearly six out of ten projects are led by very small businesses, SMEs or startups. Large listed companies such as L’Oreal SA and Airbus SE will also take part in the conference with factory project announcements.

title: China’s next AI deals clouded by selloff after Anthropic IPO
article:
(Nov 23): A selloff in global stocks that’s accelerated since the record US initial public offering of Anthropic PBC is clouding the outlook for the next wave of share sales by China’s artificial intelligence champions.

DeepSeek, Moonshot AI and StepFun are among Anthropic’s direct competitors weighing or preparing share sales. While their plans don’t hinge entirely on the performance of the Claude chatbot maker’s shares, the faltering global AI trade is adding complexity for the highly anticipated listings. Their timing and pricing may also be impacted by investors having to contend with a changing regulatory backdrop and steep losses on earlier deals.

Anthropic’s $119.5 billion deal became a catalyst for a scathing selloff across AI stocks, triggering deep losses in several markets in Asia. For China in particular, the trade that once made the country’s technology giants some of the world’s most coveted stocks has turned into a US$1.7 trillion rout. The feverish pace of IPOs has slowed and former standouts like Z.AI Co and CXMT Corp have struggled.

“In the second half of 2026, the AI fever has cooled in midst of the market volatility, as investors focus more on return on investment,” said Thea Jamison, the New York-based managing director of Change Global Investment. “The overall IPO market in China has abated, as both the China Securities Regulatory Commission and HK’s Securities and Futures Commission have asked banks and intermediaries to improve deal quality.”

AI fundraising helped lift Hong Kong first-time share sale proceeds to a six-year high of US$52.3 billion, making 2026 the second-best year on record and putting 2010’s US$57.8 billion peak within sight.

See also: US probing alleged spy tied to ex-Nvidia CEO, spy chief says

But some recent deals already showed how quickly AI euphoria can turn. Z.AI and MiniMax Group Inc were among the first generative AI firms to list in Hong Kong in January. Shares of Z.AI plunged more than 85% from their June peak after soaring 2,000% in less than six months. Its smaller rival MiniMax broke below its issue price this month.

Anthropic’s first two days as a public company were a microcosm of the same dynamic after the company shattered records with its IPO and rose into the ranks of the most valuable in the world. Its shares surged 17% from the offer price in their debut to give it a US$1.8 trillion fully diluted market value. But they fell 8.5% on the second day of trading, swept up in a global selloff that had the MSCI All Country World Index on course for its longest losing streak since September 2023.

See also: Tower Records becomes latest Japan retailer hit by data breach

Regardless of the market fluctuations, just having the market leader traded publicly — possibly followed by OpenAI next year — can help the share sale plans of other model makers by setting benchmarks and helping investors understand their dynamics, said Kieron Poon, investment director of Asian equities at Aberdeen Investments.

“This better-than-fear valuation should give support to overall tech sector sentiment,” Poon said. “It also may foster OpenAI’s IPO process. After that, the market may have less concern about the transparency of annual recurring revenue among global LLM as their reporting standard will align further.”

The China Securities Regulatory Commission gave informal instructions to investment banks about pausing IPOs, the Financial Times reported this month, citing three unidentified people with knowledge of the discussions.

Kimi K3 developer Moonshot has closed a final private round at a valuation of about US$50 billion and is heading towards a Hong Kong IPO in the first quarter, seeking to raise as much as US$5 billion, people familiar have said. DeepSeek is also eyeing a landmark listing in early 2027. The startup was close to securing at least 80 billion yuan (US$12 billion) in its latest round, well above its initial 50 billion yuan target, people familiar said in October.

Infinigence AI, a Shanghai-based AI cloud infrastructure provider backed by Tencent Holdings Ltd and Baidu Inc, has filed confidentially for a Hong Kong listing that could come in the first half, Bloomberg reported. Another Shanghai-based startup, StepFun, is also considering raising about US$500 million.

“In the near term, I don’t anticipate the return of IPO fervor in China/Hong Kong until the market sentiment improves,” said Jamison. “That said, Moonshot AI’s IPO has been in the works and should be the most anticipated AI name in the near term.”

title: ABB buys German cooling firm Ziehl-Abegg for US$2.2 bil
article:
(Nov 23): ABB Ltd agreed to buy privately held German cooling systems company Ziehl-Abegg SE for an equity value of US$2.2 billion.

Ziehl-Abegg is expected to generate around US$1.4 billion of revenues in 2026 and “complements ABB’s existing motors and drives portfolio with fans and integrated motors,” according to a statement Monday. ABB said it valued Ziehl-Abegg at US$2.65 billion including debt.

The transaction is expected to generate a return on invested capital “well above its weighted average cost of capital,” the Swiss company said.

ABB’s latest deal continues its acquisition spree even after it had to put the disposal of its robotics business on hold. The sale of the US$5.4 billion unit to SoftBank was halted by a Chinese government body that scrutinises foreign investments.

ABB said it intends to retain Ziehl-Abegg’s headquarters in Kuenzelsau, Germany.

title: Malaysia palm oil industry says CPO tax-waiver window has passed
article:
(Nov 23): Malaysia’s palm oil industry says the window in which an export tax waiver would have helped boost shipments and ease a buildup in stockpiles has passed.

The sector has urged the government to announce a decision on the proposed exemption to end market uncertainty, according to the Malaysian Palm Oil Solidarity Group, which comprises 14 associations spanning plantations to downstream processors.

“The window in which an exemption could have helped has passed and an exemption now would not bring a positive effect,” Malaysia Estate Owners’ Association President Ahmad Zachry Anifah Aman said in a statement on behalf of the group on Monday (Nov 23), without elaborating why. Nevertheless, a clear decision would help to end speculation and allow the industry to plan accordingly, he added.

The world’s second-largest palm oil producer has been considering temporarily nixing export duties as a way to encourage buying and drawing down inventories that are at a record high due to stronger-than-expected production. The buildup has raised concerns about storage constraints in parts of the country and the risk that mills could eventually curb purchases of fruit from smallholders.

A waiver would likely have limited impact at this point as seasonal production is expected to ease and demand is set to pick up in the coming months. Buyers and consumers of the edible oil will be preparing for Lunar New Year and the Islamic fasting month of Ramadan in February.

Plantation and Commodities Minister Noraini Ahmad said on Oct 29 that her ministry had consulted the industry and would provide its analysis to the Finance Ministry, which has the final say on the waiver.

See also: El Niño set to crimp palm oil output in 2027, squeezing supply

Palm groups have been pressing the government for a verdict following the consultation, arguing that weeks of uncertainty have prompted speculation and clouded the market outlook. The Solidarity Group wrote to Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim asking to clarify the government’s position, Ahmad Zachry said in the statement.

Benchmark palm oil futures in Kuala Lumpur extended losses to a fifth day on Monday, heading for the lowest close since March. Prices have tumbled about 18% from their September high as a deepening Malaysian supply glut and concerns over overseas demand pressure the market. Traders have also cited uncertainty over the proposed tax waiver as a drag on sentiment.

Meanwhile, overseas demand is showing further signs of weakening. Cargo surveyors reported lower Malaysian shipments in the first 20 days of November while Chinese buyers have cancelled some palm oil cargoes due to their own high inventories and storage constraints.

title: Bitcoin ETF exodus gathers pace, removing key source of support
article:
(Nov 23): Investors are pulling money from US-listed bitcoin exchange-traded funds at a faster pace, removing a key source of support for the beleaguered cryptocurrency.

The 12 ETFs saw about US$1.8 billion of net outflows last week, the most since June and the fourth straight week of withdrawals, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. Bitcoin posted its seventh consecutive weekly decline, the longest losing streak since the Terra-Luna crash in 2022. It dropped as low as US$55,254 on Saturday, the weakest since September 2024.

Bitcoin has faced several pressures in recent weeks. The US$6 billion hack of Binance at the end of October rattled crypto markets. Weakness in artificial intelligence-related trades and expectations for higher US interest rates have also hurt demand for riskier assets.

Bitcoin has steadied after last week’s sharp selloff. It was holding just above US$61,000 in Asia trading on Monday (Nov 23).

Still, pressure on the token remains high.

See also: Bitcoin extends reversal from Trump election gain to hit below US$56,000

The ETF withdrawals raise the risk of a more fragile market for bitcoin, as the funds have been an important source of demand since their US launch in 2024. So far this year, investors have pulled out over US$3.7 billion from the funds.

BlackRock Inc’s iShares Bitcoin Trust led the exodus. The fund saw a record US$544 million single-day outflow on Friday.

Most US spot bitcoin ETFs have seen outflows this month, according to Koinly CEO Robin Singh.

See also: Bitcoin options traders brace for slide to US$60,000 after selloff

“Bitcoin holding above US$60,000 is hardly convincing evidence that any recovery is underway,” Singh said. “I wouldn’t be surprised to see bitcoin slip back into the US$50,000s in the near term.”

Singh also said bitcoin could lose investor attention during the year-end holiday period, with fewer catalysts to attract fresh demand.

title: Australia to lower nominal economy estimate in budget update
article:
(Nov 23): Australia’s economy, unadjusted for inflation, will be smaller in next month’s budget update than had been anticipated in May while unemployment is expected to peak above 5%, Treasurer Jim Chalmers told parliament Monday (Nov 23).

“While revenue is a touch higher in the near term, this reflects one-off factors like strong returns in super and investment income,” the treasurer told lawmakers in a preview of the Mid-Year Economic and Fiscal Outlook. “Further out in the forward estimates, the lower nominal economy is likely to lead to substantial downgrades in receipts.”

Chalmers said the government will announce “a modest net saving” in the fiscal update while avoiding severe cuts to services. The centre-left administration has been under pressure to wind back spending to help tackle inflation, and Chalmers suggested it will try to do that.

“We understand and embrace our role in the fight against inflation,” he said. “It’s not a mini-budget full of new initiatives but it will have some budget-sized savings,” he said of MYEFO, which usually comes out in mid-December.

Australia has been running budget deficits for the past couple of years at a time when the economy was at full employment and commodity export prices were holding up, prompting criticism from some economists.

See also: Sovereign debt may not be considered the safe bet in the next decade, says former US Treasury deputy secretary

But inflation began to speed up even before the US-Israeli attack on Iran and has since been exacerbated by soaring fuel costs, prompting Chalmers and the Treasury to hunt for savings.

The Reserve Bank of Australia has run the most aggressive policy tightening campaign in the developed world this year to try to regain control over inflation, taking the cash rate to an 18-year high of 4.85% earlier this month.

That’s beginning to weigh on the economy, with the jobless rate climbing in October to a five-year high of 4.9% and household sentiment turning deeply pessimistic.

See also: UK is the ‘best house in a bad neighbourhood,’ UBS Wealth says

“Despite all of this, neither the RBA nor the Treasury are forecasting the economy to go backwards,” Chalmers said.

title: India business activity holds steady on manufacturing pickup
article:
(Nov 23): India’s private-sector activity held broadly steady in November, with stronger manufacturing offsetting weaker services activity, a flash survey by HSBC Holdings plc showed Monday (Nov 23).

The composite purchasing managers’ index edged up to 56.3 from 56.2 in October while the services PMI fell to 55.3 from 55.8. The manufacturing PMI jumped to its highest since February at 56 from 54.7 in the previous month.

“The increase in new orders was driven by stronger domestic demand, while new export orders moderated a bit,” Pranjul Bhandari, chief India economist at HSBC, said in a statement.

Services activity weakened, with the sector shedding jobs for the first time in about a year, HSBC said. Cost pressures remained subdued while businesses became more optimistic about the outlook.

The indexes, which provide an early gauge of private-sector activity, are based on preliminary survey responses and may be revised when final PMI figures are released next month. A reading above 50 indicates expansion while one below signals contraction.

See also: Tata heir questions big bets as US$185 bil group feud deepens

India’s economy has remained resilient, with data due this month expected to show growth remained close to the 7.8% pace recorded in the April-June quarter. Lower oil and gas prices could ease business costs, support margins and help sustain growth.

Indian bonds remained lower after data as investor weighed the outlook for interest rates, with the 10-year yield up 4 basis points to 7.22%.

The Reserve Bank of India is expected to raise rates further to contain accelerating inflation after increasing borrowing costs last month for the first time in nearly four years.

title: Copper falls below US$12,000 in London as metals turmoil deepens
article:
(Nov 23): Copper briefly sank below US$12,000 a tonne on the London Metal Exchange, deepening a sharp selloff as doubts grow about demand from artificial intelligence.

The red metal tumbled 9% last week as worries about the sustainability of AI spending fuelled a global rush from risk. On Monday (Nov 23), copper opened with a gain of as much as 1.5% before reversing direction and falling as much as 1.7%. Analysts warned of more uncertainty.

“Some copper bears are getting ready to exit,” said Gao Yin, an analyst at Shuohe Asset Management Co. “Others, however, think the whole AI narrative has fundamentally changed and want to stay aggressively short.”

Copper, used in the construction of data centres as well as energy infrastructure and wiring, soared to a record near US$15,000 a tonne in September on AI enthusiasm and the prospect of US import tariffs on the metal. However, the Democratic Party’s sweep of the US midterm elections has fuelled expectations for more scrutiny over the build-out, helping to send prices plunging this month.

The metal’s sharp slump last week — the third-biggest this decade — was emblematic of wider market turmoil as investors reconsidered prospects for spending on data centres and related infrastructure. Sceptics have also noted that AI is not likely to be a major driver of copper demand.

See also: Copper rout worsens as AI selloff wreaks havoc in metals markets

The mood turned markedly bearish at a major copper conference in Shanghai last week as industry participants reckoned with weak Chinese demand, a strong dollar and growing doubts over whether US President Donald Trump would impose tariffs on refined metal this year.

Expectations for import levies had drawn metal into the US and drained supplies elsewhere, buoying prices and contributing to a supply squeeze in China. By last week, traders were already preparing to ship copper out of US ports to relieve the supply pinch in Asia.

Copper fell 0.8% at US$12,069.50 a tonne on the LME as of 11.03am Shanghai time. Zinc dropped 0.7% while aluminium was up 0.1%.

title: Vietnam picks French-Korean group for high-speed rail deal
article:
(Nov 23): Vietnam has selected a consortium of eight French, South Korean and Vietnamese contractors for a VND10.24 trillion contract for surveys, feasibility study and design for the North-South high-speed railway, one of the country’s flagship infrastructure projects.

The consortium, led by France’s Systra SA, includes three South Korean firms: Sambo Engineering Co, Yooshin Engineering Corp and Korea National Railway, according to the Vietnamese construction ministry’s news website. The project management board aims to sign a contract with the group this month.

Under the 30-month agreement, the group will conduct surveys and a feasibility study, carry out front-end engineering design, known as FEED, and prepare bidding documents for the construction phase, according to state media. The work will help determine the project’s technology and investment options, providing the technical basis for subsequent implementation.

The decision marks the first concrete step in Vietnam’s push to build a roughly US$65 billion high-speed railway linking Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City, a project expected to reshape transport and economic links along the length of the country. Construction of the planned line, one of the nation’s biggest-ever infrastructure undertakings, was delayed by a year until the end of 2027 after Vietnam said in September that implementation has been slower than expected.

The group, which includes four Vietnamese companies, is tasked with identifying the route and key locations, including railway stations, bridges and tunnels. The interim report, due within the first year, must also outline technology options for the government to consider and approve.

The study must meet technical requirements while minimising disruption to local development plans and residents’ daily lives, the ministry's publication said. Thousands of people are expected to be relocated from their land to make way for the new line.

The aim is to complete the handover of land clearance to local authorities within three months of the mid-term report being approved, projected for the final quarter of 2027, the report said.

Vietnam’s parliament on Saturday passed land law amendments aimed at speeding up site clearance for projects, including the expropriation of land in ​the case of some special projects, as the government targets economic growth of at least 10% this year.

When completed, the high-speed rail project is set to have a total length of approximately 1,541km (957 miles) and reduce the journey time from the current 30 hours to around five.

title: India stocks erase yearly losses as foreign buying spurs rebound
article:
(Nov 23): Indian shares advanced on Monday, recouping all their losses this year following a return of foreign money and the recent unraveling of the AI trade that revived demand for overlooked markets.

The MSCI India Index rose as much as 0.6%, taking its rally this month to 11% and putting it on course for a fourth consecutive year of gains.

The reversal underscores how quickly India’s standing among global investors has changed. Its limited exposure to the AI investment boom contributed to months of underperformance as money chased technology-heavy markets. Now, that same trait is proving an advantage as investors pare AI exposure and look for alternatives to the global tech selloff.

Foreign buying has driven the turnaround. Global funds have poured more than US$12 billion into Indian equities in November, already a monthly record. If the momentum holds, 2026 may yet avoid becoming the worst year for foreign outflows from Indian assets — an outcome that appeared almost certain just a month ago.

title: European gas surges as cold snap threatens tight inventories
article:
(Nov 23): European natural gas jumped after forecasts for colder weather in the coming days, which could put further pressure on inventories already depleted by export disruptions stemming from the US-Iran war.

Benchmark futures surged as much as 8.6% to €96.075 (US$105.54), the biggest intraday increase in more than a week, putting the market on track for a third daily gain. European gas storage levels remain well below the seasonal average as the region heads into the peak winter demand period.

Temperatures for Northwest Europe are forecast to be about 3C to 5C below the 30-year average this week, and around 5C to 8C below normal at the start of December, data from Atmospheric G2 show. There is also a risk of lower winds around Germany, Denmark and the Netherlands early-to-mid this week, according to MetDesk, potentially crimping wind power generation.

There’s been an escalation in low-level fighting around the Middle East recently, signalling little prospect of supply disruptions easing anytime soon. While there has been a revival of crude exports from the Persian Gulf, flows of liquefied natural gas remain constrained, keeping the global market tight.

Colder weather in Asia this week could intensify competition for global LNG supply. Japan and South Korea, as well as eastern and southern China, are set to see colder than normal conditions, before temperatures climb to above-normal levels from mid-this week into early December, according to forecasts.
